title: Wave signals on 1D charts
items: Green dots under daily candles: the wave (a momentum oscillator) turns up from oversold while the 20-day average is at or below the 200-day. Red dots above: it turns down from overheated while price is stretched far above the 200-day.
Coins with a short history use the 100-day or 50-day average instead, and the card tells you which.
A card under the chart draws the wave, explains the latest dot, and will show how often they were right once the nightly backtest has enough.

title: A fresh, calmer look
items: New colours made for long chart sessions: a deep blue-grey dark mode and a soft light mode, with a quieter chart grid.
Anything you can tap or have selected is now indigo; amber only means caution (Wait, Calm, big news), so warnings stand out.
Glass top and bottom bars, softer cards, slightly bigger text, and gentler Long/Short colours.

title: Live track record on the chart
items: On 1H and 4H setups, under last night's backtest number, you now also see how the same kind of setups did in the live track record (saved every hour before the result was known).
If fewer than 100 of that exact kind have finished, it shows a wider group and says so.
Today it reads about 32% reaching target 1, slightly negative on average: a reminder that setups alone aren't an edge yet.

title: Hidden divergence and stop-hunts
items: Blue 'HDiv' marks show hidden divergence: in a trend, a pullback where RSI dips further than price, which often means the trend is about to carry on.
Amber 'Hunt' arrows show stop-hunts: price pokes past a recent high or low (where many stops sit), then closes back. The breakout failed, which often comes before a move the other way.
Each has a card under the chart explaining the latest one, and a chip to hide it. The nightly backtest measures how often they were right, including a divergence at a support or resistance level.

title: Back up your data
items: Settings → Back up your data → Save backup file. On iPhone or iPad choose Save to Files (iCloud Drive is safest).
It holds your starred markets, price alerts, imported trades, Simulator and Picks choices, and your settings.
Restore from a backup brings them back on a new Home Screen icon or another device, and you can undo it.

title: RSI divergence, and the backtest now runs experiments
items: On 1H, 4H and 1D charts, purple 'Div' marks show RSI divergences: price makes a new high (or low) but RSI doesn't follow, a sign the move may be tiring. A card explains the latest one.
Every night the backtest now also tries other stops, targets and filters on the same setups, and checks each idea on the older and the newer half of the data so luck can't fool it.
See 'What the backtest is learning' on the Simulator page. The app's rules only change when you decide.

title: A simpler Simulator
items: Results now start with a plain story in dollars: how many trades, how many won and lost, and what your account would be at the end.
A list of the latest trades says in words how each one ended, e.g. 'hit the stop' or 'reached target 2', with the dollar result.
'How a simulated trade works' explains the three usual endings. The detailed numbers are still there under 'More numbers and breakdowns'.

title: Company info on stocks, and the 200-week EMA
items: Open any stock (like Intel or Tesla) and a short card says what the company does, where it's listed (Nasdaq or NYSE), and whether the US stock market is open right now.
The stock market is open 9:30am–4pm New York time, but these futures trade around the clock, so prices can jump at the open. The card links to the exchange's page and the company's SEC filings.
Every chart now has the 200-week EMA as a dashed purple line. The top line of the chart shows its price and how far the current price is above or below it. Turn it off with the 200W EMA chip.

title: Price alerts: typo check and better catch-up
items: If an alert price is far from the current price (like $132.90 for ZEC at $1,133), the app now asks first and suggests the price you probably meant, e.g. $1,132.90.
When you switch back to the app after it was in the background, it now checks straight away whether any alert price was reached while you were away, and again every 10 minutes.

title: Price alerts
items: Tap the bell next to the star on any chart, type a price (or tap a quick one like Resistance R1 or +5%) and tap Set alert.
When the price is reached while the app is open, a banner shows at the top with a chime. Tap anywhere in the app once after opening it so your iPhone allows the sound.
If the app was closed, it checks when you open it again and tells you if the price was reached while you were away.
All your alerts are on the Starred page, where you can open or remove them.

title: Support and resistance on every chart
items: A new card under the chart shows where price sits: red resistance levels above (where rises stopped before), green support below (where falls stopped before), and how far away each one is.
Levels where price turned 3 or more times are marked strong. 'Was resistance' means an old ceiling that broke and may now act as a floor.
The same levels are drawn on the chart as S1, S2, R1 and R2. Tap the Support/Resistance chip to hide them.

title: Market light, and weekly and monthly charts
items: A coloured bar at the top of the app reads Bitcoin's daily chart, Fear & Greed and the cycle gauge: red Hot, amber Calm, purple Stormy (big swings) or green Oversold.
Tap it to see which signs counted and what Bitcoin did 7 and 30 days after past readings of the same colour. Nobody can predict the market; it's information only.
Charts now have 1W and 1M buttons. They show the big-picture trend with all your indicators, but no entry, stop or targets, since those rules were tested on 5m to 1D.

title: Download the track record as a spreadsheet
items: On the Simulator page, open the Track record's details and tap 'Download all … finished setups (CSV)'.
You get a file with every finished setup: market, long or short, entry, stop, targets, the times, how it ended and the result in R. Losses are in it too.
It opens in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets, so anyone can check the numbers themselves.

title: Company earnings filings on the News page
items: A new card on the News page links to the official earnings reports companies file with the US SEC. SoFi (SOFI) and Alphabet/Google (GOOGL) are there to start.
Each company has four buttons: earnings releases (8-K, filed on results day), the quarterly report (10-Q), the annual report (10-K) and all filings. They open on sec.gov.
Add any US-listed company by typing its ticker, and remove ones you don't need. Your list stays on this device.

title: A public track record has started
items: From now on, every Long setup and Short setup the app shows on 1H and 4H for the 25 busiest Gate markets is saved each hour, before anyone knows how it turns out.
Each one is then followed on later prices with the Simulator's rules until it hits its stop, target 2 or runs out of time. Losses stay in, and finished results are never changed.
See it at the top of the Simulator page: how many reached target 1, the average result, month by month, and the latest ten. It needs a few weeks before the numbers mean much.
These are simulated results from recorded setups, not real trades.

title: Crypto cycle gauge
items: A new gauge at the top of the News page shows where Bitcoin sits in its four-year cycle, from 0 (like past cycle lows) to 100 (like past cycle tops). Setups shows it in one line too.
It combines four price measures and the time since the 2024 halving. Tap 'The four measures' to see each one and how the gauge read at past tops and lows.
It updates once a day. It's information only and doesn't change any setup.

title: A proper guide, and a Back button in Help
items: The ? button now opens Help with three tabs: Start here, What's new and Glossary.
Start here explains what the app is, how the pages fit together, what Long setup, Short setup, Wait and No setup mean, and the numbers worth knowing.
Help has a Back button at the top that stays visible while you scroll, and your phone's back gesture closes it too.

title: Simulator: run again, clear and reset
items: Each run now clears the old result first and is labelled 'run 2 at 4:10 PM', so you can see a re-run really happened (the same settings within a few minutes give the same numbers, because the same candles are used).
New buttons: 'Clear results' under the result and 'Reset settings' next to Run.
Fixed the bottom menu bar getting stuck in the middle of the screen on iPhone after typing in a box.

title: New app icon and tidier rows
items: The app has its own icon: the amber radar on deep navy. Remove the old 'F' from your Home Screen and add the app again (Share, then Add to Home Screen) to get it.
In compact rows the tags now sit in one straight column, so tags, prices and changes line up.
'Wait' tags show a pause sign instead of an arrow, so they no longer look like 'Long'.
The 'markets up today' bar and the Compact button now share one line.

title: Fibonacci levels on every chart
items: The chart now draws Fibonacci levels from the last big move: 23.6% to 78.6% pullback levels in grey and 127.2% / 161.8% extensions in blue. Tap the Fibonacci chip to hide them.
A new card under the chart says how much of the last move price has given back, whether it has broken out, and the next level above and below.
The nightly backtest now also records where each setup sat on the last move, so you can see in the Simulator whether Fibonacci zones made any difference.
Information only: setups, stops and targets have not changed.

title: Order book on every chart
items: Each chart now shows how much money is waiting to buy and to sell near the price, the spread, and any unusually large orders.
A red note warns when the order book is thin, which means bigger spikes and worse stop fills.
Every hour the app now saves order-book depth, open interest, funding and liquidations for the top Gate markets, so the nightly test can check later whether they help.
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Simpler confirmation, based on the backtest
items: A setup is now 'confirmed' when at least one of the 4H and 1D trends agrees with it and the coin isn't being delisted.
The first nightly backtest showed setups going against both bigger trends did worst, while the other extra checks didn't help.
Liquidity and the 24-hour range are still shown on the chart, for context only.
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Your own trades, side by side with the chart
items: New on the Simulator page: load your Gate position history (CSV) to see your win rate, average win vs average loss and your biggest loss.
Breakdowns show how you did long vs short, by coin, by time of day, by weekday and by how long you held.
'Check what the chart said' shows the 1H and 4H reading at the moment you opened each of your latest 40 trades.
The file stays on your phone and is never uploaded. 'Remove my trades' deletes it.

title: Nightly test of the setups
items: Every night the app replays its own setups on the top 30 Gate markets and records what happened.
Simulator now starts with 'Last night's backtest': how often confirmed and unconfirmed setups reached target 1, with a range for luck.
Under a setup, the chart reading shows how often similar past setups reached target 1 (only once there are at least 100 of them).
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Extra confirmation before a setup
items: Every long or short setup now shows 5 extra checks: 4H and 1D trend agree, no delisting, enough trading and a normal 24-hour range. 'Confirmed' means all pass.
Setups now lists only confirmed setups. You can switch this off in Settings.
New strip on each chart: the reading on 15m, 1H, 4H and 1D side by side. Tap one to open it.
Delisting tab now also shows announced delistings from Bybit and the news, including spot delistings like EPIC's on Binance.

title: Delisting list
items: New Delisting tab on Markets: coins Binance, Gate or Bybit plan to delist, with the exchange and the date, soonest first.
Those coins get a red Delisting tag, and their chart screen shows the date at the top.
Exchanges usually close open positions at the delisting time, so it's worth checking before holding one.

title: Clearer wording and legal pages
items: 'Enter long' is now 'Long setup', 'Enter short' is 'Short setup', 'Hold' is 'Wait' and 'Avoid' is 'No setup'. Same rules, clearer wording.
'Confidence' is now 'Agreement' (same number), and 'Size this trade' is now the 'Position size calculator'.
New Terms of Use, Risk Disclosure and Privacy Notice pages (drafts for your lawyer), linked from Help, Settings and a short 'Before you start' screen shown once.
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Pull to refresh
items: At the top of any page, pull down and let go to refresh prices.
On the News page it refreshes the headlines too.
The refresh button at the top still works the same way.

title: Stress and safety check
items: The app was tested with about 3,000 markets, a flood of live prices and deliberately broken or harmful data. No way to run harmful code was found.
Fixed: one bad market from an exchange could hide that whole exchange. Now only the bad market is skipped.
Fixed: one odd headline or a broken saved setting could break a page. Both are now cleaned up automatically.
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Plan around big news
items: Setups now shows a quiet "Big news later today" line with the times of big releases still to come today, so you can plan before the 30-minute warning.
New switch in Settings: also count big Japan, China and euro-area news, like Bank of Japan or ECB rate decisions. Off by default.
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Bottom bar hides while you scroll
items: The bottom bar slides away while you scroll and comes back when you stop.
Don't like it? Settings has a switch to keep the bar on screen.
On/off settings are now slider switches.

title: New Settings page
items: Settings (the sliders button at the top right) is now a full page with your theme, row style, candle size, account size, risk %, max loss and the big news warning in one place.
Changes save as you type, on this device only.
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Safety nets
items: If one page breaks, it now shows "hit a snag" with a Try again button, and the rest of the app keeps working.
Problems are saved in Settings → App health. Tap Copy details and send them to Claude.
The app is checked automatically on every update and once every morning; you get an email only if something is wrong.

title: Big news warning
items: When a big US release like CPI, jobs or a Fed decision is within 30 minutes, an amber note shows on the signal card and the Setups page.
It tells you the time, how many minutes away it is, and when it's usually calmer to trade again.
Prices often spike both ways around these releases and stops can fill worse than planned.
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Bybit replaces Coinbase
items: Markets, prices and charts now come from Binance, Gate and Bybit.
Bybit's busiest markets and your starred ones update live every second.
4H charts on Bybit use real 4-hour candles.

title: Max-loss guard
items: New in Settings: Max loss per trade (USDT). A good start is about twice your average losing trade.
Size this trade now warns in red when a plan would lose more than that at the stop.
It also shows the smaller size and leverage that keep the loss within your limit.
Signals and stop/target levels have not changed.

title: Nightly improvements switched on
items: Claude now works on the app each night between 1am and 4am and lists what changed here.
Every update has to pass automatic tests before it goes live.
A dot on the ? button means there's something new.

title: News, bottom bar and a cleaner layout
items: News page with headlines, Fear & Greed and upcoming economic events.
Bottom tab bar, compact rows and a 24-hour mini chart on every row.
Light/dark switch in Settings; swipe back from a chart.

title: Simulator
items: Test the app's signals on the last 1,000 candles, including a top-25 stress test.
